(2) Direct URL guesses for /tierbedarf, /tiere, /haustier, /haustiere, /hunde-und-katzen, /tierzubehoer all returned 404. (3) Used the site's real search (form action /suche, param name 'anfrage', discovered from the homepage search form markup) for common German pet-product terms: 'hundebett' (dog bed) -> 5 hits, 'hundekorb' (dog basket) -> 1 hit, 'katzenklo' (cat litter box) -> 1 hit, but 'tierbedarf', 'hundenapf' (dog bowl), 'hundeleine' (dog leash) -> 0 hits ('kein Ergebnis'), and 'kratzbaum' (cat tree) -> explicit 'nicht in unserem Sortiment' (not in our range) message. None of these four products sit under any pet-specific parent node - per the boundary rules a generic branch (Kissen, Koerbe, Schuhschraenke) does not qualify as Pet Care without a pet-specific parent, so none produce an in-scope row; they are individually-tagged novelty SKUs scattered inside furniture/textile/storage categories, not a real Pet Care taxonomy branch. CONCLUSION: Hoeffner sells a small number of standalone pet-related SKUs but has never built a Tierbedarf/pet department - correctly reported as zero Pet Care rows rather than fabricating a category the site's own taxonomy does not support.
